exceptions.rationale: Affects only filelock's SQLite-backed ReadWriteLock/AsyncReadWriteLock, exploitable by a local user who can write to the lock directory. Nothing in the backend uses them: huggingface-hub takes FileLock/SoftFileLock and litellm FileLock in its proxy CLI. The fix (4.2.1) is blocked because every current litellm (1.104-1.107 pre-releases) requires filelock<4.0; bump once litellm allows 4.x.

Windows-only denial of service on the SQLite-backed ReadWriteLock/AsyncReadWriteLock by a local account; the backend runs on Linux and uses neither class. Fix (4.2.1) blocked by litellm's filelock<4.0 requirement, as for CVE-2026-112940.

Windows-only: a local account holding an oplock on a soft-lock marker stalls acquire(). The backend runs on Linux, where FileLock uses fcntl and the soft-lock oplock path does not exist. Fix (4.2.1) blocked by litellm's filelock<4.0 requirement, as for CVE-2026-112940.

Reviewed 2026-10-29; owner: @eneo-ai/core-maintainers. The symlink-to-SQLite flaw requires ReadWriteLock/AsyncReadWriteLock. Eneo has no filelock calls; its locked runtime dependents (huggingface-hub 1.21.0 and litellm 1.104.7) use only FileLock/SoftFileLock, never those SQLite classes. Fixed in 4.0.9, blocked by litellm 1.104.7 requiring filelock<4.0. Remove when a compatible fixed version can be installed; reassess if dependency versions or lock call sites change.

Reviewed 2026-10-29; owner: @eneo-ai/core-maintainers. WindowsFileLock ignores mode and inherits directory ACLs. The packaged backend/worker use the Debian Linux image in backend/Dockerfile, so the affected Windows lock implementation is not selected. This exception does not cover a native Windows deployment. Fixed in 4.2.1, blocked by litellm 1.104.7 requiring filelock<4.0. Remove when a compatible fixed version can be installed; reassess before changing the production platform.

Reviewed 2026-10-29; owner: @eneo-ai/core-maintainers. A crafted SQLite lock database can stall ReadWriteLock/AsyncReadWriteLock beyond its timeout. Eneo has no filelock calls; its locked runtime dependents (huggingface-hub 1.21.0 and litellm 1.104.7) use FileLock/SoftFileLock and do not open SQLite lock databases. Fixed in 4.2.1, blocked by litellm 1.104.7 requiring filelock<4.0. Remove when a compatible fixed version can be installed; reassess if dependency versions or lock call sites change.

Reviewed 2026-10-29; owner: @eneo-ai/core-maintainers. UnixFileLock can truncate/chmod a file another local account renames or hard-links onto the lock path. Hugging Face's FileLock path is reachable, but the operator confirmed Linux containers with the cache accessible only to Eneo backend/worker, not shared with unrelated users or processes. Uploads use server-generated staging filenames; the bundled tool runtime has a separate filesystem. The required attacker-controlled cache entry is therefore absent in this deployment. Reassess before sharing the cache, widening access, or executing untrusted code in backend/worker. Fixed in 4.2.1, blocked by litellm 1.104.7 requiring filelock<4.0; remove once a compatible fixed release is installable.

Reviewed 2026-10-29; owner: @eneo-ai/core-maintainers. SoftFileLock can accept a forged PID in a writable marker and remove a live lock. Hugging Face's FileLock uses mode 0664 and may fall back to a soft lock, so Linux alone does not exclude this flaw. The operator confirmed that only Eneo backend/worker can access the cache in the Linux deployment; unrelated users/processes cannot rewrite its markers. Reassess before sharing the cache, widening access, or executing untrusted code in backend/worker. Fixed in 4.2.1, blocked by litellm 1.104.7 requiring filelock<4.0; remove once a compatible fixed release is installable.

Reviewed 2026-10-29; owner: @eneo-ai/core-maintainers. A local attacker able to create/remove soft-lock markers can exploit inode reuse during stale-lock cleanup to admit two holders. Hugging Face's soft-lock fallback remains possible, but the operator confirmed Linux containers with the cache accessible only to Eneo backend/worker, not shared with unrelated users or processes. The attacker cannot plant or remove cache markers, including when backend/worker contend for the same lock. Reassess before sharing the cache, widening access, or executing untrusted code in backend/worker. Fixed in 4.2.1, blocked by litellm 1.104.7 requiring filelock<4.0; remove once a compatible fixed release is installable.
